Element UI Locale Dependency

Source: R/el_dependencies.R
el_locale_dependency.Rd

Element UI's own build defaults to Simplified Chinese for every component's built-in text – a pagination control's total, a date picker's buttons, a select's placeholder, a table's empty message. Loading a locale file and calling ELEMENT.locale() switches all of it.

Usage

el_locale_dependency(locale = NULL)

Arguments

locale

Language to switch to, such as "en", "fr" or "zh-TW". NULL or "zh-CN" leaves Element's built-in Simplified Chinese.

Value

A list of htmlDependency objects, or NULL for the built-in locale.

Details

el_page() and use_element() ask for English unless told otherwise, so a page built from this package's English documentation reads in English. All 59 of Element's locales are bundled; el_locales() lists them.

Examples

el_locales()
#>  [1] "af-ZA"   "ar"      "az"      "bg"      "bn"      "ca"      "cs-CZ"  
#>  [8] "da"      "de"      "ee"      "el"      "en"      "eo"      "es"     
#> [15] "eu"      "fa"      "fi"      "fr"      "he"      "hr"      "hu"     
#> [22] "hy-AM"   "id"      "is"      "it"      "ja"      "kg"      "km"     
#> [29] "ko"      "ku"      "kz"      "lt"      "lv"      "mn"      "ms"     
#> [36] "nb-NO"   "nl"      "pl"      "pt"      "pt-br"   "ro"      "ru-RU"  
#> [43] "si"      "sk"      "sl"      "sr"      "sr-Latn" "sv-SE"   "sw"     
#> [50] "ta"      "th"      "tk"      "tr-TR"   "ua"      "ug-CN"   "uz-UZ"  
#> [57] "vi"      "zh-CN"   "zh-TW"  

# English is the default
el_page(el_select("city", choices = c("Beijing", "Shanghai")))
